item.title: ▶ A household income of ₹1.5 lakh might sound like a lot. But once you add a home loan, a car EMI, your…
item.dc:creator: Zero1 by Zerodha · Instagram
item.description:
A household income of ₹1.5 lakh might sound like a lot. But once you add a home loan, a car EMI, your child’s education, and the responsibility of taking care of ageing parents, how much money is actually left?

And when you want to buy something for yourself, like a bike worth ₹70,000, how do you know if you can afford it?

Because earning more doesn’t always mean having more money to spend.

In this episode of Zero1 Alpha, we break down the financial decisions that come with managing a household, balancing responsibilities, and making room for the things you want.

From EMIs to everyday expenses, we explore how to think about money without getting lost in the numbers.

What would you like us to discuss next? Tell us in the comments!

item.title: ▶ Even a SIP can be a risky investment....
item.dc:creator: Zero1 by Zerodha · Instagram
item.description:
Even a SIP can be a risky investment.

Starting a SIP is a good habit, but where you invest your money matters just as much.

Let’s say you’re saving up to buy a bike in two years. You invest in an equity mutual fund, but just when you need the money, the market falls. You might have to sell your investments at a loss or postpone your purchase.

That’s why it’s important to match your investments with your financial goals.

For shorter-term goals, you can consider relatively safer options like liquid funds, short-duration funds or FDs. For longer-term goals, equity could be an option, depending on your risk appetite.

Want to understand how to start investing from scratch? Comment ZERO1 and we’ll send you our full video.
